name: Lunar Prospector
best_known_for: NASA Discovery polar orbiter — neutron-spectrometer hydrogen finding at both poles 1998; deliberate Shoemaker impact ended mission 1999
credit: The third NASA Discovery-class mission and the first dedicated US lunar mission since Explorer 49 (1973). Launched 1998-01-07 on an Athena II from Cape Canaveral, Lunar Prospector was captured into lunar orbit on 1998-01-11 and lowered to a 100-km polar mapping orbit on 16 January. Its neutron spectrometer detected sharp neutron-flux deficits over both lunar poles (Feldman et al., 1998 / 1999) — consistent with 10–300 million tonnes of water ice (1998 estimate) in permanently shadowed polar craters. The gravimeter, magnetometer, gamma-ray and alpha-particle spectrometers also delivered global maps of crustal composition and remnant magnetism. End of mission 1999-07-31: deliberately impacted in Shoemaker crater hoping to release a detectable water-vapour plume; none was seen (the lithium-7 fluorescence experiment that would have detected it was a long shot). The hydrogen finding stood until LCROSS (2009) and Chandrayaan-1 / M3 (2009) provided independent confirmation.
